pos.personaBrief: No verified Flamengo evidence; from general knowledge, Coutinho's Flamengo dominated games with the ball around Zico and Júnior, consistent with the verified Total Football-inspired philosophy (Brazil 1977).

pro.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, his side moved the ball fast and vertically with quick transitions, but built from the back with technical players.

est.personaBrief: Verified: Total Football-inspired model (Michels), which implies fluid interchange of positions; Flamengo's midfield and forwards rotated and overlapped.

lar.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, Flamengo attacked mostly through a technical, central trio with full-backs overlapping, not through hugging wingers.

blo.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, Coutinho's pressing and physical-preparation approach, linked to Total Football, meant a high, compact, pressing team.

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, Coutinho championed zonal marking and space occupation, in line with the Total Football model.

pla.personaBrief: Verified: he took command and tried to implement his own philosophy (1977); Flamengo played its own way regardless of opponent.

res.personaBrief: Verified titles (Carioca 1978/79, Brasileiro 1980) with an attacking philosophy; he was a pragmatic modernizer who still wanted to win by playing proactively.

sis.personaBrief: Verified: he imposed his own philosophy, a system-driven coach; but with Zico he had a star embedded in a collective with duties for all.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, he was a physical-education-trained coach emphasizing fitness and intensity, while fielding technical players like Zico.

bas.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, the Flamengo core (Zico, Júnior, Adílio, Leandro, Andrade) was home-grown and young, mixed with signings.

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, he was a disciplined, authoritative, military-trained coach (the 'captain') who set equal rules, though he built a united group.
